subject: Life Skills
title: Reciprocity
description: A micro-lesson that makes Reciprocity usable.

hook.text: A Hare Krishna member gave people a free flower at the airport. Donations skyrocketed. The flower was the trick.

buildup.text: Reciprocity is hardwired. When someone gives you something, your brain feels an obligation to give something back.

discovery.text: Robert Cialdini's research showed that even unwanted gifts trigger the urge to reciprocate.

twist.text: Scammers exploit this. A small unexpected gift — free trial, free ebook — creates a sense of debt you feel you must.

climax.text: Use reciprocity ethically. Offer genuine help first — advice, introductions, small favors — with no strings attached.

punchline.text: Give first. The world gives back naturally.

quiz.question: Why does reciprocity work even with unwanted gifts?
options: People feel grateful regardless of the gift's value
The brain creates a sense of obligation to repay any gift, wanted or not
Unwanted gifts are always more expensive
